boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Tulane rituals, celebrations and school-spirit practices rooted in campus and New Orleans culture.

cards.title: Toss beads onto the Bead Three
cards.subtitle: Academic Quad near Gibson Hall
cards.notes: Bring a strand of Carnival beads and try to land it on one of the three steel trees; admire the installation from the quad without climbing it.
cards.short_summary: Tulane preserved its bead-tossing ritual in a trio of steel trees after the original oak was removed.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane says the Bead Three replaced the original Bead Tree and continues the campus tradition of tossing Carnival throws onto its branches.
cards.source_title: Tulane Traditions: Celebrating the Green Wave Spirit
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus installation; observe posted campus access guidance.

cards.title: Join the Crawfest campus festival
cards.subtitle: Uptown campus · spring
cards.notes: Check the festival announcement for the year’s schedule, then experience its live music, local vendors and student-produced event programming.
cards.short_summary: A student-run spring festival built around crawfish, music and local vendors.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane states that Crawfest began in 2007 and has grown into a student-run campus festival with music, vendors and crawfish.
cards.access_notes: Annual event; consult the official event listing for current attendance and entry details.

cards.title: Start with Hullabaloo Hello
cards.subtitle: New-student orientation · uptown campus
cards.notes: New undergraduates can use the orientation schedule to follow move-in, welcome programming and the lead-up to the President’s Convocation.
cards.short_summary: Tulane’s named orientation welcome connects move-in week with Convocation.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane identifies Hullabaloo Hello as its orientation experience for new undergraduate students, running from move-in through the President’s Convocation.
cards.access_notes: For new undergraduate students; follow current orientation instructions.

cards.title: Second line after Convocation
cards.subtitle: President’s Convocation for New Students
cards.notes: After the ceremonial welcome, follow the brass band with the new class to the block party and stay with the official campus procession.
cards.short_summary: A New Orleans-style brass-band procession follows Tulane’s new-student Convocation.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane says students follow a traditional New Orleans brass band in a second line to a block party after Convocation.
cards.access_notes: Part of new-student Convocation programming; follow staff directions and the published schedule.

cards.title: Personalize a second-line umbrella
cards.subtitle: From Convocation to Commencement
cards.notes: Use a plain umbrella received around Convocation as a canvas for colors, memories and mementos, then carry it in the graduation celebration.
cards.short_summary: Students transform plain Convocation umbrellas into personal keepsakes for Tulane celebrations.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane states that students receive plain umbrellas around Convocation and personalize them throughout their Tulane experience.
cards.access_notes: Use only in designated event settings and follow ceremony guidance.

cards.title: Learn the Hullabaloo Cheer
cards.subtitle: Green Wave games and university celebrations
cards.notes: Read the official words before a game or celebration, then join the call with the crowd when it is led by campus spirit groups.
cards.short_summary: Tulane’s signature call-and-response school cheer is used at games and celebrations.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane’s official traditions page lists the Hullabaloo Cheer and says Tulanians recite it at games and university celebrations.
cards.access_notes: Join only when appropriate for the event; official lyrics are published online.

cards.title: Sing the Tulane Fight Song
cards.subtitle: Green Wave athletics and campus celebrations
cards.notes: Use the official song page to learn the words, then listen for the band and sing along during Green Wave game-day traditions.
cards.short_summary: The fight song ties athletic spirit to Tulane’s olive green and blue identity.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane’s official traditions materials identify the Tulane Fight Song as a song shared at games and university celebrations.
cards.access_notes: Official lyrics and audio are available on Tulane’s songs-and-cheers page.

cards.title: Return for Wave Weekend
cards.subtitle: Homecoming, Reunion and Family Weekend
cards.notes: Watch the official schedule as it is released, then choose an all-ages campus program, reunion event or the Homecoming football game.
cards.short_summary: Tulane combines Homecoming, reunions and Family Weekend into one annual fall celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane describes Wave Weekend as its combined Homecoming, Reunion and Family Weekend celebration.
cards.access_notes: Annual fall event; individual activities may require registration or tickets.

cards.title: See the Tipping Point during Wave Weekend
cards.subtitle: Wave Weekend · New Orleans
cards.notes: Review the official Wave Weekend program for current performers and entry details; the concert’s proceeds support Tulane scholarship programs.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Wave Weekend concert that pairs live music with scholarship fundraising.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane’s Wave Weekend site says the Tipping Point returns for its 10th year in 2026 in support of Tulane scholarship programs.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for November 6, 2026 at the Orpheum Theater; check official event details for entry requirements.

cards.title: Watch the Newcomb Daisy Chain procession
cards.subtitle: Under the Oaks ceremony · commencement week
cards.notes: Attend the official Under the Oaks program when eligible or invited, and look for the junior-class procession carrying the chain of more than 1,000 daisies.
cards.short_summary: A Newcomb commencement tradition carries a daisy chain assembled by the junior class.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane reports that Under the Oaks opens with a Daisy Chain of more than 1,000 daisies gathered by members of the junior class, continuing an early Newcomb tradition.
cards.access_notes: Part of Newcomb Institute’s commencement-week ceremony; consult current ceremony information.
